subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and which parts should instead be plugin, SDK, or ClawHub-owned?
rationale: The safety goal fits current priorities, but implementing it touches storage policy, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-vs-plugin boundaries that require maintainer intent before a safe implementation can be queued.

options.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
options.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific audit/review classifications to plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Build a core-owned temp artifact registry and cleanup/janitor policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader storage and cleanup responsibility in core.

options.title: Keep only narrow concrete bugs
options.body: Decline the broad default model and keep focused cleanup issues such as backup or session temp sweeps separate from workflow janitors.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific audit/review classifications to plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest product-scope signal from the related ClawHub decision and recent temp-boundary history.
